_note: Faction selection, the illustrated intro and the court introduction for the three playable houses (docs/world-bible-v2.md §7.1 and §5; Stage A, 2026-10-06). Texts follow the world bible; art slots point at images not made yet (placeholder frames are drawn until they exist: res://assets/intro/<house>_<n>.png). The court introduction is a placeholder until the character system (Part 4).

houses.culture_summary: Cold forests, moors and longhalls under grey stone castles. The North keeps the old oaths, mans the Greywall with its sons and bends the knee to the Throne in Caeloth.
houses.tradition: Holy warriors and castles: more Throne Church influence, stronger fortress defence, and the best knights in Aldryn.
houses.start: Frosthold and its valley, small and humble, in the shadow of the Greywall.
houses.pressure: The Wall needs men and the orcs beyond it are restless. House Dunmoor's drunkard lord has made his people desperate enough to call for a liberator.

intro.text: Beyond the Greywall the snow has gone silent. The Wardens send fewer ravens every winter, and those that come ask for men.
In Frosthold the hot springs still steam beneath the pale Hearthtree. Edric Varn, the Winter Shield, kneels there before every war, and the Throne has never found him wanting.
The Oath of Stillwater is void. The North will be held by whoever is strong enough to hold it. Let it be Varn.

houses.culture_summary: Fields, vineyards and paved roads under a warm sky. The great families of the south trade votes in the Senate at Crownhaven and read the omens of the Seven before every war.
houses.tradition: The Senate and patronage: influence over the other families, marriage alliances, and the discipline of the legions.
houses.start: One estate-city, Varrenum, beside Crownhaven: small and humble.
houses.pressure: Unite the families under one house before another does. The Tullan heir murdered his father, and his clients would welcome a new patron.

intro.text: The Senate House still stands on the third hill of Crownhaven, but its benches are full of men who sell their votes by the season.
Lucan Varrenus, the Silver Tongue, believes the old empire can live again under one house. He has only to persuade the rest of them, or bury them.
Corvinus holds the capital. Aemerius owes you a marriage. The Seven are watching. Speak well.

houses.culture_summary: White harbour cities, olive hills and gold mines along the western sea. Proud city-states with their own patron gods and oracles, forever trading, forever quarrelling.
houses.tradition: Trade and the sea: richer trade, stronger navies, and the gold of the mines.
houses.start: Goldspire Rock, the colossal golden sea cliff with its mines: small, but rich.
houses.pressure: Unite the free cities into one league before the dark elves pick them apart. Silverfall's council was murdered by the Lannetids, and its people want them gone.

intro.text: Black sails have been seen off the Grey Stacks again. The reavers of Brinecrag never come for the cities that are strong.
Kallias Aurekos, the Gold-Handed, rules a single rock, but the rock is full of gold, and gold buys ships, friends and silence.
Theros is a friend. Kyme is not. Silverfall is waiting for someone to cast out its tyrants. The coast could be one league, under one name.

court: Your court gathers: the founder's family, his captains and advisers. The court, family tree, marriages and heirs arrive with the character system; for now the founder leads your first army.
